patterns.name: Ranked horizontal bar
patterns.reader_question: Which entity is largest on one measure, and by how much?
patterns.relationship: Magnitude ranking of comparable entities on a single measure and status.
use_when: Every bar shares one unit, one definition and one status (for example committed, not announced)
Rank order itself matters to the argument
avoid_when: Values mix statuses or bases — use status-separated-capital or parallel-basis-panels
Fewer than three entities — state the comparison in the title or use a two-value callout

data_contract.notes: Measure, unit and status, shown as the series name
Displayed decimals; defaults to 0
Unique entity label
Magnitude on the shared basis
At most one highlighted result

patterns.units: One unit and status for every bar; zero baseline.

editable: Bar values and labels through Edit Data (embedded workbook)
Bar colours, gap width, data-label format
Frame text: title, subtitle, interpretation, source
not_data_bound: Highlight colour is a per-point fill; re-sorting after a data edit is manual

patterns.table_alternative: A two-column table (entity, value) when exact figures matter more than rank, or when there are more than twelve entities.
variations: Vertical columns for up to six short labels
Ranked dot plot (ranked-dot) when bars would be visually heavy
limitations: Does not show uncertainty, status mix or change over time

excluded_alternatives.reason: Angles compare magnitudes less accurately than aligned bar lengths and fail beyond a few categories
Perspective distorts length; prohibited by the exhibit rules

patterns.name: Ranked dot plot

patterns.relationship: Ordered comparison of single values on a shared axis that may start above zero; position, not length, carries the value.
use_when: Bars would exaggerate small differences because every value sits far from zero
The reader needs the ordering and approximate gaps, with the axis range stated
avoid_when: The measure is an additive quantity whose size relative to zero matters — use ranked-bar
Items are measured on different bases or in different units

data_contract.notes: Measure and unit
Stated axis range; every value must fall inside it
One dot per item
At most one accent dot

patterns.units: One unit and basis throughout; the non-zero axis range is printed on the slide.

not_data_bound: Dot positions are drawn on a computed scale; values are not data-bound and there is no embedded workbook

patterns.table_alternative: A sorted table of item and value, with the measure and basis in the header.
variations: Two-period dots on the same rows (dumbbell)

limitations: The axis does not start at zero, so gaps must not be read as proportions

patterns.name: Grouped bar

avoid_when: Series are parts of a whole — use a composition form
There are more than three series or six categories — use a table or small-multiples

Series names, in legend order
